issues.detail: The Hebrew 'וְשִׁית עַל עָפָ֥ר בָּ֑צֶר וּבְצ֖וּר נְחָלִ֣ים אוֹפִֽיר' is a poetic line (Job 22:24) meaning 'and place [your] gold in the dust, and [the gold of] Ophir among the stones of the brooks.' The Chinese renders 'בָּצֶר' (gold, treasure) as '比色城' (a city name 'Bizeth'?), and 'אוֹפִיר' (Ophir, a place known for gold) as '俄斐' (Ophir) but misconstrues the syntax: the Hebrew has 'place gold on the dust' and 'Ophir [gold] among the stones of the brooks' — the Chinese says 'spread its dust on the city of Bizeth, and pile its valley's rocks into Ophir,' which reverses the imagery and adds a city name not in the text. The meaning is substantially altered.
